chief_complaint: large localized painful swelling on arm after bee sting
hpi_details: A 74-year-old female presents to the clinic with large localized painful swelling on arm after bee sting. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks the bee left its stinger festering deep under her skin, or that bacteria from her garden soil got into the puncture wound.
concerns: She is terrified that the expanding redness means the sting has turned into blood poisoning that could spread through her bloodstream.
expectations: She hopes the doctor will check if the stinger is still buried inside her arm and prescribe strong antibiotics to clear up the inflammation.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Large Local Reaction to Insect Sting (non-anaphylactic) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Large Local Reaction to Insect Sting (non-anaphylactic) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Bee Sting Allergy localized: Cold compresses, oral antihistamines, elevate arm, reassure, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Large Local Reaction to Insect Sting (non-anaphylactic).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Anaphylaxis (if any systemic symptoms present) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Any hives away from the site, wheeze, or dizziness — reclassifies this as anaphylaxis.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.diagnosis: Large Local Reaction to Insect Sting (non-anaphylactic)
teaching.one_liner: An exaggerated but localized inflammatory response to a bee or wasp sting — swelling larger than 10cm confined to the sting site, without systemic involvement.
differentials: Anaphylaxis (if respiratory, circulatory, or severe gastrointestinal symptoms are present)
red_flags: Any hives away from the site, wheeze, or dizziness — reclassifies this as anaphylaxis

must_ask.say: How large is the swelling, and is it staying around the sting site?
Any hives elsewhere on your body, wheezing, or feeling faint?
When were you stung, and has the swelling been getting bigger since?
Is the area warm, red, or draining pus — or has a fever developed?
Have you had a large local reaction to a sting before?

history.answer: I was stung by a bee on my left forearm yesterday, and now my arm is really swollen, red, and painful.
It happened yesterday afternoon around two o'clock while I was working in the garden, and the swelling started shortly after and slowly expanded.
The sting is on the back of my left forearm, but the redness and swelling spread halfway up my arm toward the elbow.
It feels like a throbbing, burning ache that feels very tight, around a five out of ten in severity.
The swelling has been steadily getting larger since yesterday afternoon, and it hasn't started to shrink yet.
Letting my arm hang down or bumping it hurts worse, while resting it on a pillow brings a little relief.
I have been feeling unusually tired and sluggish since yesterday evening, but I don't have any body aches.
No, the rash and swelling are only on my left arm, with no hives or itchy spots anywhere else on my body.
No, my breathing is completely normal, with no shortness of breath, wheezing, or chest tightness.
No, my lips, tongue, and throat feel completely normal, and I have no difficulty swallowing.
No, I haven't had any dizziness, lightheadedness, or feeling like I might pass out.
No, I have had no nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, or diarrhea.
No, I haven't had any fever or chills, although the swollen arm itself feels quite warm.
No, there is no pus draining from the sting site and no red streaks spreading up my arm.
I was pruning some rose bushes in my backyard when a bee flew out and stung me on my bare arm.
I was stung once many years ago, but it was just a tiny bump that cleared up in a couple of days.
I washed it with soap and water and put a cool washcloth on it, but I haven't taken any pills or ointments.
It is difficult to use my left arm to carry things or do chores, and the tightness made it hard to sleep comfortably last night.
I thought maybe the stinger is still stuck deep under my skin and festering, or that dirty soil from my garden got into the sting and caused an infection.
I'm terrified this redness is turning into blood poisoning, because the hot red patch keeps creeping further up my arm every hour.
I was hoping you could check if the stinger is still buried in there and give me a course of antibiotics to kill the infection.
I don't have any chronic medical illnesses like high blood pressure, diabetes, or heart disease.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter painkillers, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or environmental triggers.
I have never smoked in my life.
I only drink a glass of wine on special family occasions, maybe once every few months.
I am retired and spend my time gardening, and I live at home with my husband.
No one in my family has a history of severe allergies, asthma, or unusual swelling reactions.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/78 mmHg, heart rate 76 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Alert elderly female resting comfortably without acute respiratory distress or facial swelling.

Large, well-demarcated area of erythema and tense edema measuring roughly 12 by 8 cm over the left forearm, warm and tender to touch with a central punctum, without fluctuance, purulence, or streaking, and no generalized hives.
No uvular deviation, lip swelling, tongue enlargement, or posterior pharyngeal edema.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally on auscultation without wheezing, stridor, or rhonchi.
Regular heart rate and rhythm with normal heart sounds and no murmurs.
Radial and brachial pulses are intact and brisk bilaterally with capillary refill under two seconds.
Left elbow and wrist have slightly reduced active range of motion due to soft tissue swelling, with no joint line tenderness or joint effusion.
No palpable cervical, supraclavicular, or axillary lymphadenopathy.
